title: Why a business plan matters

match.reason: No point in the bank covers the purpose of a business plan; the closest ones, on establishment and growth or entrepreneurship, are related ideas rather than the same one.

draft.title: Why a business plan matters
card: A business plan is a written document that sets out what a business wants to achieve and how it will get there.
It guides decisions. Owners and managers can check a choice against the plan and ask if it moves the business toward its goals.
Lenders and investors often ask to see a plan before they provide finance. It shows them the business has clear goals and a realistic way to reach them.
A plan also gives a standard to measure against. The owner can compare what happened with what was planned and then make changes.
draft.remember: A business plan sets out goals and how to reach them, so it guides decisions and helps win finance.

a.q: Why would a bank ask a new business owner for a business plan before approving a loan?
opts: It shows clear goals and a realistic way to reach them
It guarantees that the business will make a profit
It removes the need for the owner to make decisions
It lets the bank manage the daily running of the business
a.why: A lender wants evidence that the business has goals and a workable way to reach them, and a plan provides this. A plan does not guarantee profit, because results can differ from what was planned.
a.clue: Think about what a lender needs to feel confident about.

b.q: Priya runs a bakery in Bathurst. A supplier offers her a cheap oven that would let her sell wholesale, but her plan aims to grow her own shopfront sales. How does the plan help her decide?
opts: She can check if the oven moves her toward her plan's goals
She must refuse the oven, because a plan cannot be changed
The plan will tell her the exact price to pay for the oven
The plan will find a lender to pay for the oven
b.why: A plan gives a standard to test a choice against. Priya can ask if wholesale selling fits her goal of shopfront growth. A plan guides decisions but does not forbid change, and it does not set prices or find finance by itself.
b.clue: Use the plan to test the choice, not to make it for her.

a.best: It shows clear goals and a realistic way to reach them

b.best: She can check if the oven moves her toward her plan's goals
